subject: Acme long-context eval — next steps & model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme long-context eval — next steps & model recommendations

Hi Sam / Li —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- You want a summarization pipeline that handles long legal transcripts (~80k tokens per doc) and produces executive summaries that preserve decision points.
- Tolerance for minor wording differences is medium, but you need high fidelity for action items and dates.
- Latency SLOs: sub-2s per 1k tokens for interactive review; batch jobs can be longer.
- Data controls: must run in VPC/protected environment for initial pilot.

Recommended evaluation plan (what we'll run for the pilot):
1) Long-context eval: run summarization + truncation stress tests using a representative set of 50 transcripts (we discussed 60–90k token range).
2) Models to benchmark: Redwood-Long-65B-q4 (primary), Redwood-Chat-13B-long (fallback, cheaper), and an off-the-shelf Llama-2-70B variant for comparison.
3) Metrics: ROUGE-L / LongR metrics for content retention, hallucination rate on named entities, and truncation point behavior (where output fidelity drops).
4) Prompt sets: we will use the prompt-set attached (acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl) and run a sweep of temperature/presence_penalty settings.

Deliverables & timeline: 
- I’ll share the initial prompt set and a benchmark harness by EOD 2026-03-02. (attached: acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl)
- Our SE (Neha) will run a baseline long-context eval and share results + a short summary PDF by 2026-03-03. (expected: acme-long-context-benchmarks.pdf)
- Schedule technical deep-dive to review regression cases and quantization/latency tradeoffs: propose 2026-03-04 10:00 PT.

Open questions for you:
- Do you have a smaller subset (5–10 docs) we can use for an initial quick pass with redactions?
- Any constraints on model families (open-source only vs proprietary) for the pilot environment?

If that all looks good I’ll kick off the eval tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl

- Ballpark cost delta: for a pilot of ~50 docs (avg 80k tokens input + 1k output) run once, the 65B q4 candidate is likely ~2.5–3x the per-token cost of the 13B fallback; exact numbers depend on batching and KV cache reuse — we'll include a detailed cost estimate in the PDF.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme long-context eval — next steps & model recommendations

Hi all —

Quick technical notes from the baseline runs I kicked off this morning (high-level, more detail in the Drive):

- Setup: ran 3 models (Redwood-Long-65B-q4, Redwood-Chat-13B-long, Llama-2-70B) across the 8 redacted transcripts. Sequence lengths peaked ~89k tokens.
- Truncation behavior: for the 13B model we saw deterministic truncation at ~32k tokens without prefix caching enabled. With prefix/KV caching and our continuous batching enabled the 65B candidate maintained fidelity up to ~120k tokens before we observed meaningful drop in recall for late-document action items.
- Summarization fidelity: ROUGE-L and manual spot checks show the 65B-q4 preserved 94% of action-item mentions, 13B-long preserved ~78%. Llama-2-70B was comparable to 65B on recall but had higher latency and lower throughput in our harness.
- Hallucination / named entities: overall low for all models on the redacted set; a few missing dates where source text used shorthand — we flagged these as prompt engineering cases (we can add a pre-pass normalizer).
- Quantization caveats: Q4 gives good memory savings; watch out for slight tokenization edge cases on very long sequences — we'll add tokenization consistency checks to the harness.

Next steps I recommend:
- Run a 50-doc sweep (our full long-context eval) with the 65B-q4 and Llama-2-70B to validate the pilot numbers.
- Add a post-processing validator that checks extracted dates / entities and backfills from the source if ambiguous.
- We'll capture a per-token cost estimate for each model with expected batching and ideal KV reuse.

I've uploaded initial CSV logs and a one-page summary to the Drive (acme-long-context-benchmarks.pdf). I’ll expand the benchmark report after the 50-doc run.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
